about: What the provider's website may run on this computer through the command relay. Anyone who acts as the account's owner on the provider's site can queue a command, so this list is decided here, in the build, and not by what a plugin says about itself. A connector with an entry gets exactly the verbs it lists. A connector with no entry gets only the verbs its plugin declares and does not journal (its reads). Everything else can only be run from OAIY on this computer. Nothing here can be widened by a plugin's manifest, and there is no wildcard: a verb is reachable when it is named.

aokie.about: The phone bridge. Allowed: what the provider's call console, its flows and its MCP connector_command queue to run the phone line (answer, reject, hang up, speak, dial, text) and the status reads that front-desk staff are granted. Not allowed, on purpose: everything FormLogic keeps for its Device Admin role, which is set up at the computer (dongle drivers and certificates, the dongle reset and preferred dongle, phone pairing and connecting, settings, consent, the outbox) and every read of them, and the three verbs nothing on FormLogic's side queues (call.switchboard, call.activate, sms.thread). Evidence is the formlogic.com repository at commit 12275d2e, paths from its root; link/policy.rs tests check that every listed verb has evidence and that no evidence is left for a verb that is not listed. FormLogic itself keeps call.remoteStatus, call.assistance.respond, call.takeOver, call.resumeBot, call.endCaller, call.declineWaiting and remote.* off the relay (formlogic/backend/src/Services/DesktopCommandService.php:42-49), and none of them is listed here.
